webster.text: A joining; union; amity; as the juncture of hearts.

more.text: A union of two bodies; a seam; particularly, a joint or articulation.
The line or point at which two bodies are joined.
A point of time; particularly, a point rendered critical or important by a concurrence of circumstances.

example.quote: Henry judging that, at such a juncture, he should gain more by clemency and indulgence, than by rigor and severity.
